tasks.short: Develop a new drink: gather ideas, draft the recipe, test and taste it, cost it and write the recipe card.

steps.what: Bartender gathers ideas from trends, seasonal ingredients and guest requests
Bartender drafts drink recipes with quantities on paper

loop.input: The bartender's brief (base spirit, flavour direction, glass, target price) and the bar's ingredient list with costs and allergen tags.
loop.output: Three recipe variants with quantities in millilitres and a method line.
loop.check: Only ingredients on the bar's list may appear; pour cost and allergen tags are computed from list prices and ingredients, not taken from the draft. The bartender reads each variant against the brief and drops any whose combination does not make sense; only variants they would actually mix go to tasting.
loop.stop: Three variants per brief, one redraft; then the bartender writes the recipe.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposing balanced combinations from a flavour direction is creative drafting; a cost calculator only checks a recipe that already exists.

steps.what: Bartender mixes test versions, tastes and adjusts proportions
Bartender works out pour cost and sale price: in a spreadsheet today; after the change pour cost is computed in the recipe system and the bartender sets the sale price
Bar manager tastes the drink and approves recipe and price

Bartender writes the recipe card with method, glass, garnish and allergens: by hand today; after the change quantities and allergen lines fill from the approved record and the bartender writes method, glass and garnish
Bartender checks the final recipe card against the tested drink: quantities, method, glass, garnish and allergen lines
Bartender publishes the checked recipe card to the team's recipe tablet

tasks.design: Drink recipes live in the recipe system ({OTHER}) with ingredient costs and allergen tags; a bounded model step drafts three variants from the bartender's brief using only the bar's own ingredients, and costing, allergens and VAT treatment are computed. The bartender tests and tastes and sets the sale price, the bar manager approves, and the card fills quantities and allergen lines from the approved record; the bartender writes method, glass and garnish, checks the card and publishes it to the team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recipes lived on paper and in heads, so every new drink was costed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe tools hold costs and allergen data per recipe, pour-cost calculators set prices from a target, and language models draft combinations a calculator can check.
tasks.still_hard: Taste and balance are only found by mixing and tasting; drafts can be unbalanced or derivative.
tasks.human_edge: Tasting, balancing and giving a drink a story guests remember.

ambition.what: A seasonal drink tested every month instead of twice a year.

tasks.altitude: The bartender starts from costed drafts and spends the time tasting; the bar manager approves from a complete record.

reach.learn: Whether the same costed draft step works for coffee recipes.

evidence.claim: A recipe tool costs each recipe from ingredient prices and stores allergen and dietary data per recipe.
A free calculator adds pour cost per ingredient and gives the menu price for a target pour-cost percentage.
Cocktails carry 21% VAT on the alcoholic part and 9% on the rest only if the drinks are also sold unmixed and the prices add up.
Guests must be informed about 14 allergens in unpacked food and drinks.

assumptions: Boundary: from the idea to the approved recipe card; putting the drink on the menu is outside.
Input contract: ingredient list with unit cost and allergen tags, kept by the bar manager in the recipe system from supplier prices; fallback is the spreadsheet.

Gathering ideas, tasting, the manager's approval, checking and publishing the card keep their full time. s2 keeps 75 because choosing the combination stays with the bartender and only writing out variants with quantities drops. s4 keeps 20 for setting the sale price. s6 keeps 50 because quantities and allergen lines fill from the record and the bartender still writes method, glass and garnish.
Bar manager time is outside the bartender's savings.
unknowns: Whether the bar keeps recipes in a system.
How many new drinks are developed per year.
research_questions: How often does a drafted variant survive the tasting with small changes?

already_counted.description: Bartender reads the drafted variants against the brief and picks those to test.
Bartender writes method, glass and garnish into the approved record.

incremental.description: Bartender adds new ingredients with cost and allergens to the list.
Bar manager keeps ingredient prices current.

approvals.approved_version: The recipe card with quantities, method, glass, garnish and allergen lines exactly as checked by the bartender in s6c, published once to the team's recipe tablet for that drink; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the bartender does not use the drafts and ingredient prices are often out of date, so s2 keeps 100 and s4 keeps 40 (14.8); high: drafts are used and prices are current (21.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead the bar team during a shift: brief, assign stations, watch service and responsible serving, train and report.

steps.what: Head bartender briefs bar staff on specials, stations and stock issues
Head bartender assigns stations and breaks to bar staff during the shift
Head bartender supervises the work of other bartenders: speed, pouring, service
Head bartender checks age checks and refusal of service to intoxicated guests
Head bartender trains new bar staff on recipes and procedures
Head bartender reports staff issues of the shift to the bar manager

Head bartender records each bartender's actual hours: typed into a message today; after the change the rostered times show in the scheduling app and the head bartender corrects them to the hours actually worked
Head bartender checks the shift's hours per bartender against who actually worked and the breaks taken
Head bartender confirms the checked hours to the bar manager in the scheduling app

tasks.design: A shift briefing note is generated from the {OTHER} point-of-sale system (specials, sold-out items, large reservations) for the head bartender to use at the briefing; recipe cards sit on a tablet behind the bar for training. The scheduling app shows the rostered times, the head bartender corrects them to the hours actually worked, checks them and confirms them once instead of typing a message; staff issues are still reported as today; supervision and responsible serving stay fully with the head bartender.
tasks.previous_blocker: Little blocked it: supervising a bar is live, in-person work.
tasks.enabler_now: Tills can export the day's specials and sold-out items; recipe cards and hour approvals are standard app features.
tasks.still_hard: Watching quality, keeping order and refusing service are judgement calls in the moment.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the room, backing up staff with a difficult guest and teaching by example.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less time on notes and messages.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of food preparation and serving workers
reach.learn: Whether the generated briefing note serves floor and bar alike.

evidence.claim: Till systems can export the day's specials and sold-out items into a briefing note.
Serving alcohol to minors or intoxicated guests is forbidden, and bar supervisors need a social hygiene qualification under national rules.
Per-bartender sales logs in the till can count as a facility to monitor performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: one shift's supervision from briefing to the shift report; rostering is outside.
Input contract: specials and sold-out items set in the till by the bar manager and kitchen; recipe cards from the recipe system; fallback is the head bartender's own notes.
No per-bartender performance view is added.

Supervision, station choices, responsible serving, reporting staff issues and checking and confirming hours keep their full time. s1 keeps 80 because the note gathers specials, sold-out items and reservations the head bartender now collects by asking around. s5 keeps 90 because trainees look up recipe cards on the tablet instead of asking for each one. s6h keeps 70 because only the rostered times fill in.
unknowns: How much of the shift the head bartender spends serving versus supervising.
research_questions: Do recipe cards behind the bar shorten training of new staff?

already_counted.description: Head bartender checks the generated briefing note before the shift.

incremental.description: Head bartender keeps the recipe tablet charged and current.

approvals.approved_version: The shift's actual hours per bartender exactly as checked by the head bartender in s6c, confirmed once in the scheduling app for the bar manager's pay run; any correction needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the briefing note is often incomplete and trainees still ask for every recipe, so s1 keeps 95 and s5 keeps 100 (1.1); high: note and recipe tablet are used as designed (4.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count bar stock, order or requisition liquors and supplies, receive deliveries and report errors.

steps.what: Bartender counts bottles, kegs, mixers and glasses after closing
Bartender writes the order of liquors and supplies against par levels
Bartender checks the final wholesaler order: items, quantities against the count and the budget, and the wholesaler account
Bartender places the checked wholesaler order through the wholesaler's webshop: by e-mail or phone today, by one release after the change
Bartender checks the brewery lines: kegs, quantities and the delivery day
Bartender phones the checked brewery order to the brewery
Bartender receives deliveries and puts them away in the cellar and bar
Bartender checks deliveries against the order and notes short or wrong lines
Bartender reports missing or wrong items to the supplier: by phone today; after the change a message is drafted from the ticked-off lines and the bartender adds what is wrong
Bartender checks the complaint: lines, quantities, what is wrong and the supplier it goes to
Bartender sends the checked complaint to the supplier

tasks.design: The bar counts on a tablet in shelf order in the stock module of the {OTHER} point-of-sale system, which proposes an order from par levels and expected use from drinks sold; orders above the weekly budget are blocked for the bar manager. The bartender adjusts the proposal, checks the wholesaler lines and releases them once to the wholesaler's {PARTNER_PORTAL}, and checks and phones the brewery lines. Deliveries are ticked off on the tablet, and short or wrong lines are drafted into a complaint that the bartender checks and sends.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts and orders were on clipboards, and each supplier was called or e-mailed separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Till stock modules hold par levels and drink recipes, and drinks wholesalers take orders through webshops.
tasks.still_hard: Counting partly used bottles stays manual; small breweries and local suppliers take orders by phone.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the weekend's events and which drinks will run, and spotting a damaged delivery.

ambition.what: Liquor ordered twice a week against expected use, so less cash sits on the shelves.

tasks.altitude: The bartender confirms orders instead of building them; budget decisions stay with the bar manager.

reach.learn: Whether the same counts feed the supervisor's variance view.

evidence.claim: A recipe tool links recipes to ingredient costs, giving the per-drink quantities that expected-use estimates need.
Till stock modules can propose orders from par levels and counts.
The tax authority advises a reliable register and keeping records for seven years.

assumptions: Boundary: from the closing count to deliveries checked and errors reported; paying invoices is outside.
Input contract: par levels per item set by the bar manager in the stock module; drink recipes in millilitres from the recipe records; fallback is the clipboard.
Orders above the weekly budget go to the bar manager outside this flow.
Scenario: the main wholesaler takes webshop orders; breweries are still phoned.

Receiving and putting away (s4), phoning breweries, the checks and the complaint send keep their full time. s5 keeps 80 because only finding the paper order drops; noting each difference is still the bartender's own record. s3 keeps 10 for the release and its follow-up. s6 keeps 50 because the lines and quantities fill from the tick-off and a message replaces a call.
unknowns: Whether the till has a stock module.
Number of suppliers the bar orders from.
research_questions: How much stock value does the bar carry today against weekly use?

already_counted.description: Bartender reviews and adjusts the proposed order.

incremental.description: Bartender fixes failed webshop orders and missing articles.
Bar manager keeps par levels and recipes current.

approvals.approved_version: The wholesaler order lines with items and quantities exactly as checked by the bartender in s3c, sent once through the wholesaler's webshop; any change needs a new check.
The brewery order with kegs, quantities and delivery day exactly as checked by the bartender in s3d, phoned once to the brewery; any change needs a new check.
The complaint with lines, quantities and what is wrong exactly as checked by the bartender in s6c, sent once to the supplier of that delivery; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the stock module proposes poor orders for slow sellers and half of wholesaler lines still need a call, so s2 keeps 60 and s3 keeps 50 (20.7); high: the proposal is used and the webshop takes the wholesaler order (31.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the bar menu: review sales and margins, choose drinks, cost and price them, write descriptions and publish.

steps.what: Bartender reviews sales and margins per drink from the till
Bartender plans bar menus: which drinks to keep, drop or add
Bartender costs and prices the new line-up: in a spreadsheet today; after the change margins are computed from the recipe records and the bartender sets the prices
Bartender writes menu descriptions and allergen information: by hand today; after the change allergen lines fill from the records and descriptions are drafted for the bartender to check and rewrite

loop.input: The chosen line-up, the house recipe records and the bar's house style for menu text.
loop.output: One draft description per drink, with allergen lines and VAT codes taken from the records.
loop.check: Allergen lines and VAT codes come from the records, not the draft. A check lists any ingredient, garnish or claim in a description that is not in that drink's recipe record. The bartender reads each description against the recipe and rewrites what does not match; unclear ones are written by hand.
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft per drink; then the bartender writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Short descriptions in the house style are prose; a template fills allergens but not the description.

steps.what: Bar manager approves the menu, prices and allergen text
Bartender checks the final menu before release: line-up, prices, descriptions and allergen lines exactly as approved, and the till and QR menu it goes to
Bartender publishes the approved menu: updates till items and the printed and QR menus by hand today; after the change one release updates till items and the QR menu and makes the print file
Bartender briefs bar staff on the new menu

tasks.design: A menu view built on till sales and recipe costs sorts drinks by popularity and margin; the bartender chooses the line-up and sets prices, and margins, allergen lines and VAT codes are computed from the records. A bounded model step drafts a description per drink from the house recipe, a check lists anything not in the recipe, and the bartender rewrites what does not match. After the bar manager approves line-up, prices and menu text, the bartender checks the final menu and releases it once to the {OTHER} point-of-sale items and the QR menu, and the print file is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales, costs and menu text lived in different files, so menu changes were rare and slow.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe tools sort dishes in a profitability matrix, QR menus update from the till, and language models draft line-ups a calculator can check.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a menu that fits the bar's identity is taste; local promotion rules differ per city.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the guests and building a menu with a story and a sense of place.

ambition.what: Bar menus refreshed each season with margins checked on every drink.

tasks.altitude: The bartender chooses between costed drafts; costing, allergen text and publishing disappear. Price approval stays with the bar manager.

reach.learn: Whether the same popularity-margin view and draft step suit food menus.

evidence.claim: A recipe tool sorts dishes in a profitability matrix and stores allergen data per recipe.
A QR menu linked to the till shows descriptions and allergen information and sends orders through the till.
Amsterdam bans prices for alcoholic drinks below 60% of the usual price for 24 hours or less since 1 April 2022.
In 2022 only 41% of 9,407 inspected hospitality businesses complied with allergen information rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from reviewing sales to the menu published and staff briefed; developing new drinks is outside.

Input contract: till sales per drink; recipe records with costs, allergens and VAT treatment kept by the bar manager; local promotion rules entered by the bar manager; fallback is the spreadsheet menu.
Bar manager time is outside the bartender's savings.

Choosing the line-up, the approval, the check before release and the staff briefing keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 because the view replaces compiling sales and costs by hand. s3 keeps 20 for setting prices. s5 keeps 60 because allergen lines fill from records and drafts save some writing, but each description is read and often rewritten. s6 keeps 10 for the release and checking the till afterwards.
unknowns: Whether all drinks are in the recipe records with costs.
How often the bar menu changes today.
research_questions: Do seasonal menus with checked margins raise bar margin over a year?

already_counted.description: Bartender reads the menu view before planning.
Bartender reads drafted descriptions against the recipes, rewrites what does not match and checks allergen lines.

incremental.description: Bartender keeps descriptions and records consistent and reports bad drafts.
Bar manager keeps promotion rules and price targets current.

approvals.approved_version: The menu with line-up, prices, descriptions and allergen lines exactly as approved by the bar manager in s4 and checked by the bartender in s6c, released once to the till items, the QR menu and the print file; any change needs a new approval and check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many drinks are not yet in the recipe records and drafts are mostly rewritten, so s1 keeps 60 and s5 keeps 85 (34.5); high: records are complete and drafts used (43.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The bartender keeps mixing, tasting, serving and leading the bar; costing, counting sheets and menu admin shift to records and drafts.
reach: Food service supervisors' liquor variance checks
skills_to_grow: Keeping recipe records with costs and allergens accurate
Judging drafted recipes and menus by taste and margin
Confirming order proposals with local knowledge
role.ambitious_version: A bartender who refreshes the menu each season with tested drinks and checked margins, and orders against real use.
